items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Arstella Whitthers, who meanwhile on the suggestion of Lily, had changed her name for the pseudonyme of Martine Kay, had been engaged for the tour.

ctx.x: We started rehearsals the next day. We had also engaged a young French musician from Toulouse, Guy Lafitte. He was 21 years old and played the tenor and clarinet. The previous year, he had made a concert with Mez Mezrow and Zutty and had got good reviews from the jazz critics.

Arstella Whitthers, who meanwhile on the suggestion of Lily, had changed her name for the pseudonyme of Martine Kay, had been engaged for the tour. But a few weeks before, she wrote that she was ill and could not make the tour. Lily tried to get in touch with her immediately as we had started to advertise her, but she couldn't be found nowhere. What had happened was that the girl had fallen in love and would not leave her boy friend for several months. Lily was very sore for business reasons and also because…

Somebody signalled us that there was a singer named Miriam Burton in town. Miriam had been the leading singer in Katerine Dunham's group fo singers and had beautiful suprano voice. She was not a jazz singer really, but on ballads, she was wonderful. So, we engaged her also.
